tasks.desc: Project scaffolding: Initialize Electron + Svelte + Tailwind CSS + electron-forge project. Set up package.json with all dependencies (electron, svelte, tailwindcss, pdf-lib, pdfjs-dist, vitest, electron-forge with svelte template). Configure electron-forge for Linux x64 builds. Set up Tailwind config. Create basic main process (main.js) with BrowserWindow loading Svelte app. Create base Svelte entry point (App.svelte) with a simple 'Signaturizer' header. Configure Vitest for testing. Set up dev scripts (start, test, build). Create proper .gitignore. Verify the app launches with 'npm start' showing a window.

Image Processing Library: Create src/lib/image-processor.ts (or .js) with pure functions for signature image processing using Canvas API. Functions: 1) captureFrame(videoElement) -> captures current video frame to canvas. 2) cropImage(imageData, rect) -> crops rectangular region. 3) removeBackground(imageData, threshold) -> converts to grayscale, removes pixels above threshold (white/near-white) by setting alpha to 0, returns processed ImageData. 4) applyColorTint(imageData, color) -> tints non-transparent pixels to specified color preserving alpha/luminance. 5) processSignature(videoElement, cropRect, threshold) -> combines all steps into one pipeline. Write comprehensive unit tests in src/lib/__tests__/image-processor.test.ts using Vitest. Test cases: bg removal on synthetic images, crop accuracy, tint color application, edge cases (all-white, all-black images). All functions must be pure/testable without Electron.

Signature Store/Persistence Library: Create src/lib/signature-store.ts with CRUD operations for signature library. Data model: { id: string(uuid), name: string, imageData: string(base64 PNG), createdAt: ISO string, updatedAt: ISO string }. Functions: 1) loadSignatures() -> reads from JSON file in Electron userData path. 2) saveSignatures(signatures) -> writes to JSON file. 3) addSignature(name, imageData) -> generates id, timestamps, adds to store, returns new entry. 4) deleteSignature(id) -> removes by id. 5) updateSignature(id, updates) -> updates name/imageData, bumps updatedAt. 6) getSignature(id) -> returns single entry. The store should handle missing/corrupt files gracefully (return empty array). File path: path.join(app.getPath('userData'), 'signatures.json'). For testability, accept a file-system adapter interface so tests can use in-memory storage. Write comprehensive unit tests in src/lib/__tests__/signature-store.test.ts.

PDF Viewer Component: Create src/lib/pdf-viewer.ts and src/renderer/components/PdfViewer.svelte. The library module wraps pdf.js: 1) loadPdf(arrayBuffer) -> returns PDFDocumentProxy. 2) renderPage(pdfDoc, pageNum, canvas, scale) -> renders page to canvas element. 3) getPageCount(pdfDoc) -> returns page count. The Svelte component renders a PDF in a scrollable container: - Accepts pdfData prop (ArrayBuffer) - Manages pdf.js document loading - Renders current page to a canvas element - Navigation controls: prev/next buttons, page number display (e.g., '3/10'), click to go to page - Zoom controls: zoom in, zoom out, fit to width, fit to page - Scroll support for zoomed pages - Emits events: pageChange(pageNum), zoomChange(scale) - Exposes methods: getCurrentPage(), getZoom(), getCanvasCoordinates(clientX, clientY) for mapping mouse position to PDF coordinates - Responsive canvas sizing Write unit tests for the library module (mock pdf.js). Component testing can be basic (verify it mounts).

PDF Export Engine: Create src/lib/pdf-exporter.ts using pdf-lib. Functions: 1) exportSignedPdf(originalPdfBytes, signatures) -> takes original PDF as Uint8Array and array of placed signatures, returns modified PDF as Uint8Array. Each placed signature: { page: number, x: number (PDF coords), y: number, width: number, height: number, imageData: Uint8Array (PNG bytes), color: {r,g,b} or null }. The function: loads PDF with pdf-lib, for each signature embeds the PNG image (pdf-lib embedPng), draws it at the specified page/position/size. If color is provided, tint the image before embedding (modify PNG pixels). 2) calculatePdfCoords(canvasX, canvasY, canvasWidth, canvasHeight, pdfPageWidth, pdfPageHeight) -> converts canvas pixel coordinates to PDF coordinate space (PDF origin is bottom-left). Write thorough unit tests: create a test PDF, embed a signature, verify output is valid PDF, verify signature appears at correct position. Test coordinate conversion. Test with multiple signatures on different pages.

Main UI Shell: Build the main application layout and window structure. Update App.svelte to be the root layout: - Top toolbar bar with: File menu area (Open PDF, Export), Sign button (placeholder), page navigation area (placeholder) - Main content area that fills remaining space (will host PdfViewer) - Status bar at bottom (optional, for helpful messages) - Use Tailwind CSS for clean, modern styling. Light theme. Colors: white/gray backgrounds, subtle shadows, rounded corners. Create src/renderer/components/Toolbar.svelte with the toolbar layout and button stubs. Wire up IPC handlers in main process: - open-file-dialog -> shows native open dialog filtered for .pdf, returns file path - save-file-dialog -> shows native save dialog for .pdf, returns save path - read-file -> reads file at path and returns ArrayBuffer - write-file -> writes data to path - get-user-data-path -> returns Electron userData path Set up preload.js to expose these IPC methods via contextBridge. Verify the app launches with toolbar visible, buttons are styled, and IPC channels work (test with console.log or a test button).

Camera Capture Modal: Create src/renderer/components/CameraModal.svelte. This is a modal overlay (centered, with backdrop) that opens when user clicks 'Create New' in signature dropdown. Features: 1) Requests camera access via navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ video: { facingMode: 'environment', width: { ideal: 1280 }, height: { ideal: 720 } } }) 2) Shows live camera feed in a video element 3) Horizontal alignment guide line (dashed, centered) to help user hold paper level 4) Camera selection dropdown if multiple cameras available 5) 'Capture' button - freezes current frame, switches to crop/edit mode 6) Crop mode: overlay a resizable rectangular selection box on the captured image. User drags corners/edges to define crop area. Show dashed rectangle. 7) Below the crop area: threshold slider (0-255, default 200) with live preview of processed signature (bg removed) 8) 'Done' button -> emits event with { capturedImageData, cropRect, threshold } 9) 'Clear' button -> resets to live camera feed 10) 'Cancel' button (X) -> closes modal, emits cancel event Props: isOpen (boolean). Events: capture(data), cancel(). Style: modal with white background, subtle shadow, max-width 600px. Tailwind styling, clean and modern.

Signature Dropdown Component: Create src/renderer/components/SignatureDropdown.svelte. This is a popup/dropdown that appears when clicking the 'Sign' button in the toolbar. Features: 1) Dropdown positioned below the Sign button 2) List of saved signatures: each row shows a small thumbnail (50x30px preview of the transparent PNG) and the signature name 3) Hover over a signature row -> shows X button on the right to delete (with confirmation) 4) Click a signature -> emits 'select' event with the signature object 5) At the top/bottom: 'Create New Signature' option with a + icon -> emits 'create-new' event 6) If no signatures saved, show empty state message: 'No signatures yet. Create one!' 7) Close dropdown when clicking outside 8) Close dropdown after selecting a signature Props: signatures (array of {id, name, imageData}), isOpen (boolean). Events: select(signature), delete(id), create-new(), close(). Style: dropdown with white bg, subtle border/shadow, hover highlights, scrollable if many signatures. Tailwind.

Signature Placement System: Create src/renderer/components/SignaturePlacement.svelte. This component renders placed signatures on top of the PDF canvas and handles interaction. Features: 1) Renders an overlay div positioned exactly over the PDF canvas 2) Each placed signature is an absolutely positioned img element showing the transparent PNG 3) Click on PDF area -> places the currently selected signature at that position (centered on click point) 4) Click on an existing placed signature -> selects it (shows handles) 5) Selected signature shows 4 corner handles (small squares) for resizing 6) Drag signature to reposition (mousedown on signature body -> mousemove -> mouseup) 7) Drag corner handle to resize (maintain aspect ratio, min size 20x20) 8) Press Delete key -> removes selected signature 9) Each placed signature stores: { id, signatureId, page, x, y, width, height, imageData, color } 10) Right-click or panel: color picker for selected signature (preset colors: black #000000, blue #0000CC, dark gray #333333, plus custom picker) 11) The component coordinates with PdfViewer to get page dimensions and scroll position Props: selectedSignature (signature object or null), pdfViewerRef (reference to PdfViewer component). Events: signaturesChanged(placedSignatures[]). Exports method: getPlacedSignatures() -> returns all placed signatures with absolute PDF coordinates.

Wire Camera Capture Flow: Integrate CameraModal → Image Processing → Signature Store. Update App.svelte to: 1) Add state: showCameraModal (boolean), signatures (array) 2) When user clicks 'Create New' in SignatureDropdown -> set showCameraModal = true 3) CameraModal emits 'capture' with {capturedImageData, cropRect, threshold} 4) Pass captured data through image-processor functions: cropImage -> removeBackground -> generate final transparent PNG as base64 5) Save processed signature via signature-store: addSignature('Signature ' + (count+1), base64PNG) 6) Refresh signatures state from store 7) Close camera modal 8) The user should be able to: open app -> click Sign -> Create New -> see camera -> capture -> adjust crop -> adjust threshold -> see preview -> click Done -> signature appears in dropdown list. Wire all IPC for file system access (read/write signatures.json). Add error handling (camera denied, processing errors). Test the full flow manually.

Wire Signature Stamping and Export Flow: Integrate SignatureDropdown → Placement → Color Tinting → PDF Export. Update App.svelte to: 1) Add state: pdfData (ArrayBuffer), pdfFileName (string), placedSignatures (array), selectedSignature (for placement) 2) Wire 'Open PDF' toolbar button -> IPC open-file-dialog -> read file -> set pdfData 3) Wire 'Sign' button -> SignatureDropdown -> user selects signature -> set selectedSignature 4) When selectedSignature is set and user clicks on PDF canvas -> SignaturePlacement places it 5) Wire color tinting: when user changes color on a placed sig, apply color via image-processor.applyColorTint, update the placed signature's imageData 6) Wire 'Export' toolbar button -> collect all placed signatures from SignaturePlacement -> convert canvas coords to PDF coords via pdf-exporter -> call pdf-lib export -> IPC save-file-dialog -> write file 7) Add undo support: Ctrl+Z removes last placed signature 8) Toolbar shows current page info when PDF is open 9) Test the full flow: open PDF -> select signature -> place it -> resize -> tint color -> export -> verify exported PDF has signature

Integration Tests, Polish, and Final Touches: 1) Write integration/e2e tests for critical flows: a) Open app -> capture signature -> verify it appears in library -> close and reopen -> verify persistence. b) Open PDF -> place signature -> export -> verify exported PDF contains signature image. c) Delete signature -> verify removed from library. Use Vitest + happy-dom or jsdom for component testing. 2) Add keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+O (Open PDF), Ctrl+S (Export), Ctrl+Z (Undo), Delete (remove selected sig), Escape (deselect/close modal). 3) Polish UI: loading states, empty states, error messages, transitions/animations for modal and dropdown. 4) Add app icon and window title 'Signaturizer'. 5) Set reasonable window defaults: 1200x800, centered, min-width 800. 6) Verify electron-forge build produces working Linux x64 package. 7) Create a README.md with setup instructions, usage guide, and dev commands. 8) Git commit all changes with meaningful messages.
